title: docs(release): 0.19.0 released; Open VSX check reads the universal package at its own address
body:
Records the 0.19.0 release and fixes the one check that went red in its release run.

## The release

`v0.19.0` on `4e09cab6ea` (PR #257's merge), release run 39720213044.

- **Succeeded:** tag checks, reuse of CI run 39716712837's verified packages, the GitHub Release (46 assets), Marketplace, npm.
- **Failed:** the Open VSX job failed at its **own check**, not at publishing.
  - **Cause:** once a version has targeted packages, Open VSX's untargeted `/<version>` answer names whichever package it picks (`win32-arm64` to the script), so the universal VSIX was compared with another target's bytes.
  - **Open VSX state:** every package was uploaded, and three activated a few minutes later.
- **Checked after the run, by each target's own address:**
  - all 7 packages on the Marketplace and on Open VSX match the release assets (14 of 14);
  - npm's integrity equals the release tarball's;
  - the assets pass `SHA256SUMS`.

## The fix

`scripts/publish-registry.mjs` reads `/api/<ns>/<ext>/universal/<version>` for the untargeted package. That address also answers for versions published only universal (0.18.2).

Drill against the real Open VSX, in `docs/certification/cifinal0190.md` §21:
- the tag's check fails 3 of 3 on the universal VSIX;
- the fixed one matches 3 of 3, and still matches `win32-x64`.

## Also

- PLAN §10 `0.19.0 released` record; roadmap regenerated.
- Windows real-use record for the release (`docs/real-life/release-0.19.0-limits-W.md`): 5 calls, every one `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, $0.00.
- Two closed §7 gate records archived (byte-identical reassembly, `docs/certification/plan-archive.md`), so the record fits under `check:plan`'s gate.

Local: all 19 static gates exit 0; `publishRegistry.test.mjs` + `manifest.test.ts` 44/44; plan suites 135/135.

title: release: 0.19.0
body:
The 0.19.0 release, tagged again. Two earlier tags stopped at the release's own tag checks before anything was built or published, and both are deleted (owner's order: a failed check never moves the version):

- `v0.19.0` on `e48e8c6bce`: the browser check's runtime pin was more than 14 days behind Stable (renewed in PR #255).
- `v0.19.1` on `ff7c78d7a3`: `check-browser-runtime-pin.mjs` could not load `zod`, which it began importing in PR #255, because the tag-checks job installed nothing. No pull-request run executes that job.

## What changes

- **Tag checks and the weekly pin job install dependencies** before the pin check.
- **New gate `npm run check:workflow-scripts`** (in `quality:gates` and the hosted static gates): every `node scripts/...` step that runs before its job's install may import Node built-ins only, read through esbuild's metafile. It fails on main's workflows with exactly this defect and passes with the fix.
- **The release's Linux helper step could never have passed** (found by reviewing every job after the tag checks, none of which has run since 0.18.2): `unzip -p release/*.vsix` exits 11 with seven packages, and `dist/voiceLinux.js` is only a loader. The step now reads each VSIX's `voiceLinux.js` from its runtime archive (`scripts/runtime-archive-member.mjs`) and checks all seven against the staged helpers.
- **Recovery from a reused release now works**: the reuse job keeps the source-tree receipt, and `findRecovery` accepts a passed reuse job with a skipped build.
- Version, CHANGELOG `[0.19.0]` (both refused tags under Release infrastructure), PLAN's 0.19.0 record and the roadmap at 0.19.0.

## Proof

- Local: all 19 static gates exit 0; `npm run build` exit 0; `test/unit/manifest.test.ts` 40/40.
- Red/green drills in `docs/certification/cifinal0190.md` §15–§18:
  - the gate on the defect, and with an install removed on purpose;
  - the old helper step on PR #255's real packages (exit 11) against the new one (exit 0, seven accepted; exit 1 with one helper byte changed);
  - the old and new `findRecovery` against the real GitHub API (the reused v0.18.2 run refused, then accepted; ineligible runs still refused).
- The registries' universal-plus-targets shape, checked live on redhat.java 1.59 (Marketplace and Open VSX) for the URLs `verifyPublished` reads.

title: Release 0.19.1
body:
Release 0.19.1, the first published 0.19 release.

`v0.19.0` was tagged on PR #237's merge (`e48e8c6bce`) but never published: release run 39569020330 stopped at its own tag checks, before building anything, because the browser check's pinned Chrome for Testing runtime (154.0.8037.92) had fallen more than 14 days behind Chrome Stable (156.0.8078.47). A tag never moves (docs/RELEASING.md), so the release ships as 0.19.1.

What changes against `main`:

- The browser check's runtime pin moves to Chrome for Testing 156.0.8078.47 (r1706539, published 2026-10-20), produced by the new `scripts/pin-browser-runtime.mjs`. The generator reproduces the old 154 pin byte for byte on all four platforms before it is trusted; on Windows the real runtime store downloaded, verified, extracted and launched 156 (`browser-check-restart.mjs` and the live browser-check suites).
- `package.json` / `package-lock.json` at 0.19.1; CHANGELOG's section renamed `[0.19.1]`, with the reason under Release infrastructure and the pin under Changed; PLAN §10 records 0.19.0 as never published and prepares 0.19.1; the roadmap regenerated.

Local gates: build (bundle budgets, split, legal records) 0, the 18 pre-push gates 0, `check-browser-runtime-pin.mjs` 0.
